title: Molecular structure - 123 school
heading: Molecular structure
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.

questions.q: Explain the octet rule
questions.a: The tendency of atoms to achieve the noble gas configuration and surround themselves with 8 electrons. The number of missing electrons is "borrowed" from a bonding atom by sharing them; this number gives the number of bonds.

questions.q: Which exceptions are there to the octet rule?
questions.a: For helium, He, and hydrogen, H, the duet rule applies: in H<sub>2</sub> each H atom contributes 1 of its valence electrons. He surrounds itself with 2 of its own valence electrons. For the transition metals the 18-electron rule applies.

questions.q: Name 6 atoms for which the octet rule holds
questions.a: C, O, F, N, S, Li,

questions.q: Which atom sometimes has a different number of bonds from what the octet rule predicts?
questions.a: S

questions.q: Explain what the octet rule means for carbon
questions.a: Carbon, C, has 4 valence electrons. By forming 4 covalent bonds, C gets 8 electrons around it, for example in CH<sub>4</sub>

questions.q: Explain what the octet rule means for chlorine
questions.a: Chlorine, Cl, has 7 valence electrons. By forming 1 covalent bond, Cl gets 8 electrons around it, for example in Cl<sub>2</sub>

questions.q: How do you show non-bonding valence electrons in a Lewis structure?
questions.a: With a dot

questions.q: How do you show bonding electrons in a Lewis structure?
questions.a: Two bonding electrons as a line; in a double bond 4 electrons are involved in the covalent bond, so 2 lines

questions.q: Set out the step-by-step plan for the Lewis structure of NH<sub>3</sub>
questions.a: Step 1: N has 5 valence electrons, H has 1, so 8 electrons in total. Step 2: octet rule for N, duet rule for H. Step 3: 6 electrons (3 pairs) in 3 bonds between H and N. The duet rule for H is satisfied. 2 electrons left. Step 4: 2 non-bonding electrons give N 5 valence electrons and make the structure neutral.

questions.q: What does the Lewis structure of the ion NH<sub>2</sub><sup>−</sup> look like?
questions.a: N forms two bonds with H. The duet rule is satisfied for H. N satisfies the octet rule, with 4 electrons in the 2 covalent bonds and 4 non-bonding electrons. That gives 6 electrons for N, 1 electron more than the 5 valence electrons of N, which gives a formal negative charge on the N atom: [NH<sub>2</sub>]<sup>−</sup>

questions.q: How is the formal charge distributed in CO<sub>3</sub><sup>2−</sup>?
questions.a: C forms 4 bonds: 1 double bond with O and 2 single bonds with O. The doubly bonded O atom has 2 non-bonding electron pairs and so satisfies the octet rule. The 2 singly bonded O atoms each have 3 non-bonding electron pairs, so they satisfy the octet rule, and each of these O atoms has 1 electron more than its number of valence electrons and is negatively charged.

questions.q: What does VSEPR stand for?
questions.a: Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion

questions.q: What is the steric number of CO<sub>2</sub>, SO<sub>2</sub>, CF<sub>4</sub> and NH<sub>3</sub>?
Give the shape of molecules with a steric number of 2, 3, 4
questions.a: Linear, trigonal planar, tetrahedral

questions.q: Give the angles in degrees for molecules with a steric number of 2, 3, 4
Explain what dipoles are
questions.a: Partial charges in a molecule

questions.q: Explain what the steric number is
questions.a: The sum of the number of atoms bonded directly to the central atom plus the number of non-bonding pairs

questions.q: Does CO<sub>2</sub> have a dipole?
questions.a: No. CO<sub>2</sub> has a linear structure, there is a partial negative charge on the oxygen atoms and a positive charge on the central carbon atom, but because of the symmetry the charges cancel each other out

questions.q: Does SO<sub>2</sub> have a dipole?
questions.a: Yes. According to VSEPR, SO<sub>2</sub> has a trigonal planar arrangement. There is a partial negative charge on the oxygen atoms and a positive charge on the central S atom. Because of the non-bonding electron pair on the S atom, the molecule has a bent shape, so the negative charges do not cancel each other out. This creates a dipole

questions.q: Why does SO<sub>2</sub> dissolve well in water and CO<sub>2</sub> does not?
questions.a: SO<sub>2</sub> has a dipole. Water also has a dipole, so a dipole–dipole interaction can form between the two molecules

questions.q: Explain what resonance is
questions.a: The movement of electrons within a molecule without the molecule changing chemically.

questions.q: How can you tell from the structural formula whether a substance shows resonance?
questions.a: If you can draw several Lewis structures of the same molecule, there is resonance

questions.q: What general property do resonance structures give a molecule?
questions.a: The more resonance structures a molecule has, the more stable the substance is.

questions.q: Benzene, C<sub>6</sub>H<sub>6</sub>, has 3 double bonds. Explain how resonance works.
questions.a: Benzene has 3 double and 3 single bonds: the electrons of the 3 double bonds can move continuously, so that the single bonds become double and the earlier double bonds become single.

questions.q: How are the different resonance structures of benzene shown in one structure?
questions.a: By drawing the double bond as a circle inside the honeycomb-shaped hexagon
